agent: game options wave, reader A (the window)
question: The in-game settings window menu_settings_ingame: CSettingsScreen and CIngameSettingsScreen - construction, the six slots, show and hide, the four tabs, Apply, Back and closing, the Game tab whole, and how CFrontendSettingsScreen differs.

structs.name: CSettingsScreen
structs.comment: The settings window's code, shared by the front end's `menu_settings` and the in-game `menu_settings_ingame` (interface/settings.gui): four tabs (buttons settings_tab_1..4 showing menu_settings_GAME, _VIDEO, _AUDIO, _CONTROLS), ApplyButton and BackButton. Slot 0 the scalar deleting destructor, 1 Show, 2 Hide, 3 IsShown, 4 the per-frame copy of the three volume sliders into the settings, 5 Close (pure; each child its own). Built by CSettingsScreen::CSettingsScreen (0x6F5C00) with the window made at once and the tabs' observers attached. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-settingswindow.md, section A.
structs.evidence: RTTI: CSettingsScreen has no bases, one table 0x15D4AF0 (VA) of 6 slots, slot 5 = _purecall 0xB961D5. Size: CFrontendSettingsScreen's second base CFrontEndView sits at +0x3DC (RTTI), and the base's own code touches +0x3D8 as a float (StoreChoices 0x6F80A0, Refresh writes +0x3D8), so sizeof is exactly 0x3DC. Wrong if the RTTI base offset of CFrontEndView were not 0x3DC.

structs.name: CIngameSettingsScreen
structs.comment: The in-game settings window (`menu_settings_ingame`), held at CInGameIdler +0x1D2C, made by CInGameIdler::Enter and hidden at once; the menu's Game Options shows it. Adds only the in-game screen at +0x3DC and slot 5, CIngameSettingsScreen::Close, which goes back through CInGameIdler::CloseMenu. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-settingswindow.md, section A.
structs.evidence: Enter 0x6605DF pushes 0x3E0 to operator new and calls 0x6FB710, which writes vftable 0x15D4BC8 at 0x6FB773 and the idler (EDI) at +0x3DC at 0x6FB779, the last 4 bytes of 0x3E0. RTTI: one base, CSettingsScreen at 0, table 6 slots, slot 5 introduced. Wrong if another allocation size reached 0x6FB710 - findRefs --callers gives one caller, 0x660607.

structs.name: CFrontendSettingsScreen
structs.comment: The front end's settings window (`menu_settings`), a CSettingsScreen and a CFrontEndView (at +0x3DC, table 0x15D4B8C, whose slots 0, 2, 3 and 4 are thunks to the destructor, Show, Hide and the volume copy). Its slot 5, CFrontendSettingsScreen::Close, hides it and sends the front end back to its view 0. The front end is at +0x3E4. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-settingswindow.md, section A.12.
structs.evidence: The constructing site 0x6F3B98 pushes 0x3E8 to operator new, calls the base constructor 0x6F5C00 with 'menu_settings', then writes 0x15D4B70 at +0, 0x15D4B8C at +0x3DC and the front end (the same [esp+0x14] passed as the parent) at +0x3E0 and +0x3E4 (0x6F3C13-0x6F3C33). RTTI: bases CSettingsScreen @0 and CFrontEndView @0x3DC. Wrong if that site were not CFrontendSettingsScreen's only construction - the string menu_settings has one reference, 0x6F3BC1.

addresses.name: CSettingsScreen::CSettingsScreen
addresses.signature: CSettingsScreen* __stdcall CSettingsScreen::CSettingsScreen(CSettingsScreen* this, void* parent, Hoi3CString* windowName)
addresses.comment: **The settings window's base constructor**, for the in-game and the front-end screen alike. `this`, the parent screen (a CEU3Idler: the CInGameIdler or the CFrontEnd) and the window's name are all stack arguments, `ret 0xC`. In order: the table 0x15D4AF0, shown (+4) = 0; nineteen embedded observer glues with their handlers (button glues 0x2C bytes, vftable 0x15D4B0C; checkbox glues 0x20, 0x15D4B38; scrollbar glues 0x18, 0x15D4B58) - +0x8/+0x34 decrease/increase_resolution, +0x60/+0x8C refresh rate, +0xB8/+0xE4 multisample, +0x12C Apply (CSettingsScreen::OnApply), +0x158 Back (the shared thunk 0x6FB9A0 that calls slot 5), +0x184 CSettingsScreen::EnableButtons (attached to nothing), +0x1B0/+0x1DC/+0x208/+0x234 the four tabs, +0x260..+0x308 the Video tab's three sliders and four checkboxes, +0x370/+0x39C decrease/increase_autosave; parent at +0x120, parent slot 17 (the graphics) at +0x124, parent slot 14 (the gui) at +0x128; **the window made at once** through the gui's slot 11 with the name and parent slot 16, kept at +0x368; BackButton, ApplyButton and the four settings_tab_N attached by name (window slot 13); **+0x358 = menu_settings_VIDEO**, the tab shown first; the six resolution/refresh/multisample buttons attached on menu_settings_VIDEO and the two autosave buttons on menu_settings_GAME; then the window shown, its subwindows hidden (slot 28) and the Video tab shown; then CSettingsScreen::InitGameTab, the Video, Audio and Controls tabs' set-up (0x6F6E00, 0x6F6AB0, 0x6F6CA0) and CSettingsScreen_Refresh. Ghidra's RTTI pass calls it CSettingsScreen_2. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-settingswindow.md, section A.1.
addresses.evidence: Read whole, 0x6F5C00-0x6F685B: `mov edi,[ebp+8]` (this), `ret 0xC`; callers 0x6F3BF6 (front end, push name/parent/this) and 0x6FB759 (CIngameSettingsScreen, push eax(name)/edi/esi). Glue handlers read off the stores (`mov [edi+0x10],0x6FA5B0` etc.) and attaches off `lea reg,[edi+N]` into the element's +0x48 slot 1 after each name. +0x358 at 0x6F63FF from the menu_settings_VIDEO lookup. Ends 0x6F67F9-0x6F6844 as described. Wrong if the window slot 13/27 roles differed - both match their uses in CInGameIdler::ToggleMenu.

addresses.name: CSettingsScreen::Show
addresses.comment: Slot 1, both screens. The window (+0x368) shown (its CGuiObject's slot 13), every subwindow hidden (window slot 28), **the current tab (+0x358) shown** - the Video tab the first time, afterwards whichever tab was last chosen - then CSettingsScreen_Refresh (the Video, Audio and Controls controls set again from the settings singleton; **not the Game tab**), the window's slot 11, and shown (+4) = 1. No pause of its own. In game, CInGameIdler::OnMenuOptionsButton calls it. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-settingswindow.md, sections A.2 and A.3.

Held at slot 1 by all three tables (vtable.py --holding). Wrong if 0x6F9370 read the autosave choice - it references neither autosave_value nor +0x36C (string and displacement census of the class's code).

addresses.name: CSettingsScreen::Hide

CInGameIdler::Enter calls it straight after making the screen; CInGameIdler::CloseMenu calls it on both its arms; CFrontendSettingsScreen::Close calls it first. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-settingswindow.md, section A.2.

addresses.name: CSettingsScreen::IsShown

Asked by CInGameIdler::CloseMenu (is a subwindow up) and by UpdateTutorialAndAuxWindows every frame, which then calls slot 4. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-settingswindow.md, section A.2.

addresses.name: CSettingsScreen::UpdateVolumes
addresses.comment: Slot 4: the three volume sliders' positions (mastervolume +0x348, effectvolume +0x34C, musicvolume +0x350, each scrollbar's +0x48 slot 4) written into the settings singleton at +0x80, +0x84, +0x88 as floats. **Run every frame the in-game window is up** - UpdateTutorialAndAuxWindows (0x64FD51) asks slot 3 and then calls it - so a volume slider is heard as it moves, before Apply; CIngameSettingsScreen::Close puts the values Show saw back. CFrontendSettingsScreen's slot 4 is a jump here, and its CFrontEndView slot 4 a thunk to that. What each volume is, and whether the sound engine reads these fields at once, is reader C's (FINDINGS-settingswindow.md section C). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-settingswindow.md, section A.5.

Wrong if the three sliders were in another order - InitAudio 0x6F6AB0 stores master, effect, music at +0x348, +0x34C, +0x350 in that order.

addresses.name: CIngameSettingsScreen::Close
addresses.comment: **Slot 5, the in-game BackButton** (through the glue +0x158 and the thunk 0x6FB9A0) and the end of Apply. The volumes Show or the last Apply saw (+0x3C8, +0x3CC, +0x3D0) put back into the settings (+0x80, +0x84, +0x88) - undoing a slider moved and not applied - then CInGameIdler::CloseMenu(fromCustomGame) on the idler (+0x3DC), with fromCustomGame true only where a custom game's setup is under way (GetCustomGameSettings: byte 0 set and +0x18 below 2). CloseMenu, finding the screen up, hides the menu, hides the screen and opens the menu again on its six buttons. Nothing else is undone or applied: the Game tab's autosave choice (+0x36C) stays in the screen unapplied. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-settingswindow.md, section A.7.
addresses.evidence: 0x6FB8D0-0x6FB96E read whole: three movss pairs +0x3C8->+0x80, +0x3CC->+0x84, +0x3D0->+0x88; `call 0x41C4E0; cmp byte [eax],0; je`; `cmp dword [eax+0x18],2; jge`; `mov al,1`/`xor al,al; push eax; call 0x66BE80` with ecx = [esi+0x3DC]. vtable.py: only CIngameSettingsScreen slot 5. Wrong if +0x18 were not the setup stage - that reading is inferred (FINDINGS-leaderassign.md).

addresses.name: CSettingsScreen::OnApply
addresses.comment: **`ApplyButton`** (glue +0x12C), for every tab at once. Extent 0x6F7300..0x6F8095 with a catch funclet at 0x6F761D that resumes at 0x6F762E - **Ghidra splits it there** (Catch_All@006f761d, FUN_006f7630), trap 3. In order: (1) CSettingsScreen::StoreChoices - every tab's choices into the settings singleton, the autosave choice into +0x15C among them; (2) the display mode: the current mode's index in the settings' mode list (+0x14, 0x18-byte entries {width, height, rates}, matched on the graphics' +0x6B9BC/+0x6B9C0) and the current refresh rate's index (+0x48, searched in **entry 0's** rate list over the chosen entry's count); the multisampling (+0x54, 0 below 2 or where the table 0x170A104 marks it unsupported) set to the choice (+0x118) **where it differs, which asks for a restart**; the globals 0x170AEB0/0x170AEB4 set to the chosen mode and rate indices (+0x110, +0x114) **where either differs from the current, which asks for a restart**, else both -1; the settings' width +0x40, height +0x44 and rate +0x48 set from the choice in every case. No device reset is made. (3) **inside a try**, 0xAB1CE0 with the settings in ESI - the settings.txt writer (reader C); a throw clears the success flag. (4) BackButton and ApplyButton disabled (slot 47). (5) **On success with a restart asked**: a DefaultInfoDialog CEU3Dialog (0x68 bytes, 0x63D4B0) titled RESTART_REQ "Restart Required" with the description RESTART_REQ_DESC "You must restart the game for these changes to take effect.", brought to the front and put on the current screen's dialog list (CCurrentGameState +0xBE8, +0xA0); the buttons enabled (CSettingsScreen::EnableButtons), CSettingsScreen_Refresh, and slot 5 once - in game back to the menu's six buttons with the dialog over them. **On success without one**: EnableButtons, slot 5, CSettingsScreen_Refresh, slot 5 again - in game the second CloseMenu finds no subwindow up and **closes the whole menu**, the game left paused. **On a failed write**: a DefaultInfoDialog titled SM_ALERT "Alert", described SM_WP "Error writing to the settings-file. Check that the file is not write protected and try again", added through CEU3Idler::AddDialog; Back and Apply enabled; **the window stays open** - and the choices are already in the settings singleton for this session. `SettingsMustRestartWindow` of settings.gui is never named by the executable: this dialog is what comes up. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-settingswindow.md, section A.6.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x6F7300-0x6F8095 read whole: `call 0x6F80A0` at 0x6F732E; the mode and rate searches 0x6F7333-0x6F7443 (the rate search loads `[[settings+0x14]+8]`, entry 0's vector, at 0x6F7428); restart flag [ebp-0x11] set at 0x6F747A and 0x6F74AA; globals 0x6F7497/0x6F74A4/0x6F74B4; success flag [ebp-0x1D] = 1 at 0x6F75BC, `call 0xAB1CE0` at 0x6F760F with ESI = [0x1A863F8], cleared at 0x6F761D; slot 0xBC on both buttons 0x6F7675/0x6F76D2; branches 0x6F76F9 (failure 0x6F7BDE) and 0x6F7702 (no restart 0x6F7BC9); strings at 0x6F781D, 0x6F7977, 0x6F7CF3, 0x6F7E54; dialog slots 0x38/0x3C (SetTitle/SetDescription) and 0x24 (BringToFront); the two `call [edx+0x14]` at 0x6F7BB6 and 0x6F7BD7. findRefs --callers 0x6F7300: none direct (glue only, +0x12C attached at 0x6F6249). Wrong if 0xAB1CE0 were not the writer - that is reader C's to settle; SM_WP's text and the try are the evidence here.

addresses.name: CSettingsScreen::StoreChoices
addresses.comment: **Every tab's choices copied into the settings singleton** - the first thing OnApply does, and its only caller. In order: the Video tab's four checkbox bytes (+0x344..+0x347) into settings +0xE4 (and bit 0 of +0xEC), +0xE5 (inverted), +0xE8 and +0xE9 (with +0xEA set where it changed); counter distance from +0x3D4 into +0xFC (scaled) and counter scale from +0x3D8 into +0x100 and the global 0x170AF84; **the autosave choice (+0x36C) into +0x15C** (0x6F8189); gamma from gamma_slider into +0x5C (clamped) and handed to 0xA76810 with the graphics; the three volumes into +0x80/+0x84/+0x88 **and into the screen's saved copy +0x3C8/+0x3CC/+0x3D0**; scroll speed into +0x90 and zoom speed into +0x98 (each floored); counters_checkbox into +0xF9 (always_counters); legacy_camera_checkbox into +0x188; and every map province's weather picture marked changed. What each Video, Audio and Controls figure means is readers B's and C's (FINDINGS-settingswindow.md sections B and C); this record says only where each lands. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-settingswindow.md, section A.6.
addresses.evidence: Ghidra decompilation of 0x6F80A0-0x6F8539 and the listing's stores (`mov edi,[esi+0x36C]` 0x6F8176, `mov [eax+0x15C],edi` 0x6F8189; `fstp [esi+0x3C8/0x3CC/0x3D0]` 0x6F82FC-0x6F830B). addresses.name: CSettingsScreen::EnableButtons
